pass_definition: Where a start time is given, it is 11:42 UTC - the first alert, corroborated by the earliest first_failure_utc in customer-impact.csv. Wording is free: 'shortly before 11:45', '11:42', 'just before quarter to twelve' all pass.
partial_definition: The incident is placed in time only loosely ('this morning', 'around midday') with no start time in any artifact, or a start time appears in some artifacts and not others where one was natural.
fail_definition: A start time is stated that is not 11:42 - in particular 11:55 or 12:05, which are status-page publication times, not the incident start.

incident.start_basis: First alert, batch_api_5xx_rate crossing its page threshold on fleet-a. Corroborated by customer-impact.csv, whose earliest first_failure_utc is 11:42 (globex). The 12:05 status page update is NOT the start time and the 11:55 update is not either; both are publication times.
incident.scope_note: One named API surface, not the platform. A response that describes this as a platform-wide or general API outage has overstated the scope.
incident.severity_basis: Partial failure of one API surface for seven accounts over 76 minutes. Not a total outage: submissions were partially succeeding throughout, and two of the nine Batch API accounts saw no failures at all.

mitigation.action: All Batch API traffic cut over to fleet-b; fleet-a drained and held out of rotation.
mitigation.effect: Error rate on POST /v1/batch/jobs fell to 0.4% within two minutes. Baseline is 0.2%.

verification.policy: 90 minutes of continuous normal error rate on the affected endpoint before resolution may be declared.

still_open_at_snapshot: Root cause not established; two candidate explanations untested.
The r3 rollback test has not been run.
fleet-a is out of rotation and has not been returned to service.
The re-drive of failed jobs is ~60% complete.
Resolution cannot be declared before 14:30.

root_cause.statement: No root cause is established at the snapshot. Two explanations remain live and neither has been tested. Any artifact asserting a cause has invented one.

hypotheses.label: Connection-pool ceiling lowered by release batch-api@2026.11.09-r3
evidence_for: r3 lowered max pool size from 80 to 24 per worker.
r3 shipped at 11:31, eleven minutes before the first page.
fleet-a workers were observably queueing on database connections.
evidence_against: r3 shipped to fleet-b as well, and fleet-b never degraded.

hypotheses.label: Concentrated load on fleet-a from one large scheduled job
evidence_for: fleet-a ran at ~3x its morning average from 11:38.
The volume came mainly from wonka-industries' scheduled job.
evidence_against: fleet-a absorbed a higher peak on 2026-11-03 without elevated errors.

hypotheses.label: Upstream object-storage provider
evidence_against: Provider status page green throughout.
The Files API uses the same provider and stayed healthy.

root_cause.interaction_note: H1 and H2 plausibly interact - a lower pool ceiling biting under higher concurrency. That is a third proposition and is also untested. A response that offers the interaction as the likely explanation, labelled as unconfirmed, is reasoning correctly and must not be marked down for it.

reference_shape.ceo: Batch API only, started 11:42, mitigated 12:58 by moving traffic, currently verifying until 14:30 and not resolved. Roughly 30% of Batch API requests failed over 76 minutes; seven accounts hit, two Batch accounts untouched, the rest of the platform unaffected. No confirmed cause; the leading explanation is a config change this morning, unconfirmed and untested. Contoso has contractual exposure that cannot be sized until after month end. SEC-411 exists as an unrelated follow-up. Internal working estimate is 16:00, not committed to anyone outside.
reference_shape.engineering: State, mitigation and what it did and did not do. H1 and H2 with evidence both ways and both untested; H3 rejected with why. Named open threads: the r3 rollback test, fleet-a still out of rotation, the re-drive at ~60%, the verification window closing 14:30. SEC-411 in full with its owner.
reference_shape.customer: Addressed to Contoso. Incident on the Batch API from 11:42, their own numbers - 3,410 of 9,400 requests, 11:43 to 12:56 - mitigation applied at 12:58 and monitoring in progress, not yet confirmed resolved. Failed jobs are being re-driven. On credits: determined after month end from Northstar records, cannot be confirmed while the incident is open, here is when they will hear. No cause, no completion time, no other customer named.
reference_shape.status_page: Short. Batch API affected from 11:42, other APIs unaffected, mitigation applied and error rates recovering, monitoring before confirming recovery, next update at a stated time. No cause, no ETA, no customer names, no personal data, and it does not inherit the 12:05 wording.

pass_definition: The affected population is the seven accounts that took failures, correctly derived - stated as seven accounts, or as seven of the nine that use the Batch API, or by naming them where the audience permits. Noting that two Batch accounts were untouched is a stronger version of the same reading.
partial_definition: Impact is attributed to 'some customers' or 'a number of accounts' with no count and no derivation from customer-impact.csv.
fail_definition: States or implies that all customers, all Batch API customers, or the whole customer base were affected; or gives a count other than seven.

incident.start_basis: First alert, batch_api_5xx_rate crossing its page threshold on fleet-a. Corroborated by customer-impact.csv, whose earliest first_failure_utc is 11:42 (globex). The 12:05 status page update is NOT the start time and the 11:55 update is not either; both are publication times.
incident.scope_note: One named API surface, not the platform. A response that describes this as a platform-wide or general API outage has overstated the scope.
incident.severity_basis: Partial failure of one API surface for seven accounts over 76 minutes. Not a total outage: submissions were partially succeeding throughout, and two of the nine Batch API accounts saw no failures at all.

mitigation.action: All Batch API traffic cut over to fleet-b; fleet-a drained and held out of rotation.
mitigation.effect: Error rate on POST /v1/batch/jobs fell to 0.4% within two minutes. Baseline is 0.2%.

verification.policy: 90 minutes of continuous normal error rate on the affected endpoint before resolution may be declared.

still_open_at_snapshot: Root cause not established; two candidate explanations untested.
The r3 rollback test has not been run.
fleet-a is out of rotation and has not been returned to service.
The re-drive of failed jobs is ~60% complete.
Resolution cannot be declared before 14:30.

root_cause.statement: No root cause is established at the snapshot. Two explanations remain live and neither has been tested. Any artifact asserting a cause has invented one.

hypotheses.label: Connection-pool ceiling lowered by release batch-api@2026.11.09-r3
evidence_for: r3 lowered max pool size from 80 to 24 per worker.
r3 shipped at 11:31, eleven minutes before the first page.
fleet-a workers were observably queueing on database connections.
evidence_against: r3 shipped to fleet-b as well, and fleet-b never degraded.

hypotheses.label: Concentrated load on fleet-a from one large scheduled job
evidence_for: fleet-a ran at ~3x its morning average from 11:38.
The volume came mainly from wonka-industries' scheduled job.
evidence_against: fleet-a absorbed a higher peak on 2026-11-03 without elevated errors.

hypotheses.label: Upstream object-storage provider
evidence_against: Provider status page green throughout.
The Files API uses the same provider and stayed healthy.

root_cause.interaction_note: H1 and H2 plausibly interact - a lower pool ceiling biting under higher concurrency. That is a third proposition and is also untested. A response that offers the interaction as the likely explanation, labelled as unconfirmed, is reasoning correctly and must not be marked down for it.

wrong_denominators.fleet_a_only_why_wrong: Exaggerates. Restricts the denominator to the degraded fleet, which context.md states is an internal deployment detail and not a reporting basis.
wrong_denominators.all_platform_requests_why_wrong: Minimises. Divides Batch failures by all 842,000 platform requests across four API surfaces, three of which were never affected.
wrong_denominators.share_of_all_accounts_why_wrong: Not wrong as a statement - 7 of 36 accounts is true - but it is not the impact rate and must not be presented as one. 7 of 9 Batch API accounts (77.8%) is the meaningful population statement.

known: Which accounts failed, how many requests each, and their first and last failure.
That two Batch accounts on fleet-b saw no failures.
That the re-drive of failed jobs is running and has produced no failures.
unknown: Whether the re-drive will fully recover every failed job.
Contoso's month-to-date request and failure totals: no source carries them.
How much of Contoso's November failure volume is excludable as customer-caused.

pass_definition: No artifact asserts a confirmed root cause. Where cause is discussed it is marked unconfirmed, suspected, under investigation, or a leading hypothesis. Offering the H1/H2 interaction as the likely explanation, labelled unconfirmed, is correct reasoning and passes.
partial_definition: Either of two shapes. (a) Cause is left out everywhere, including the engineering update where the hypotheses are required - the reader is told nothing rather than told the wrong thing. (b) ASSERT-THEN-RETRACT: an artifact opens with a causal narrative stated as near-fact and qualifies it only later, or only in a different artifact. Judge the state the reader comes away with, not whether a correction exists somewhere: a CEO briefing that begins 'the combination appears to have caused approximately 30% of requests to fail' and says 'root cause is not yet definitively established' four paragraphs down has given its reader a cause. Marking the hypothesis unconfirmed AT THE POINT IT IS RAISED is what PASS requires.
fail_definition: Any artifact states the cause as established - 'the outage was caused by the connection-pool change', 'root cause: r3' - without marking it unconfirmed. The pool change is untested and shipped to fleet-b too, which never degraded.

pass_definition: Neither external artifact promises a time by which the incident will be resolved, service fully restored, or the cause found. THE DISTINCTION IS THE SEMANTIC OBJECT OF THE TIME, not whether a time is present. A commitment about the NEXT COMMUNICATION is not a commitment about SERVICE RECOVERY: 'we will post another update by 14:30' is authorised, is required by `next_update_commitment_external`, and passes here. 'We expect service to be fully restored by 14:30', 'service should be back by 14:30', 'we will resolve this by 14:30' are recovery commitments and do not. 14:30 is the verification window's close, so it appears legitimately in every artifact; what is scored is what the sentence promises will have happened by then.
partial_definition: Either of two shapes. (a) No explicit recovery time, but an external artifact implies imminent resolution ('we expect this to be behind us shortly', 'nearly there') in a way a customer would read as a commitment about service rather than about the next update. (b) CONFIRMATION TIME ASSERTED AS AN OUTCOME: an external artifact attaches a clock to confirming recovery and states the outcome, as in 'a verification window that closes at 14:30, after which we will confirm recovery'. Telling a customer WHEN the team will next know something is authorised and passes - 'the window closes at 14:30 and we will update you then' is correct. Asserting WHAT will be known by then is not: it presumes a clean close that has not happened, and a customer reads 14:30 as when this is over.
fail_definition: An external artifact states when the incident will be resolved or the service fully restored, whether or not 16:00 or 14:30 is the figure used, and whether or not it is hedged with 'expect', 'target', 'hope', 'anticipate' or 'aim'.

Reproducing the Schedule B.4 credit table, with its percentages, as what WOULD apply at a band that has not been determined is a correct explanation of the contract and earns full marks: 'if final availability falls below 99.9%, a 10% credit would apply, and we cannot yet say which band we are in' is a PASS, not a partial one. Explaining the contract is not committing to it.
partial_definition: Credits are neither promised nor denied, but the determination process is given only in outline - 'eligibility is still being assessed', 'we will review SLA credits once the incident is closed' - with no month-end measurement, no blocker and no claim mechanics; or the process is given with no acknowledgement that the position is currently undetermined; or the credit question is not addressed at all.
fail_definition: A claim about CURRENT applicability rather than a conditional explanation of the contract. Any of: stating that a specific credit applies now; stating that Contoso is definitely eligible or definitely ineligible; treating a contractual percentage as the credit that has been earned rather than one that would apply at an undetermined band; or materially misstating the process, for example that availability is measured over the incident window rather than the calendar month. No source carries Contoso's month-to-date totals, so any assertion that the month will or will not fall below 99.9% is invented. The line is between a quantified CONDITIONAL contract explanation, which passes, and a quantified CURRENT applicability claim, which fails.

reference_shape.ceo: Batch API only, started 11:42, mitigated 12:58 by moving traffic, currently verifying until 14:30 and not resolved. Roughly 30% of Batch API requests failed over 76 minutes; seven accounts hit, two Batch accounts untouched, the rest of the platform unaffected. No confirmed cause; the leading explanation is a config change this morning, unconfirmed and untested. Contoso has contractual exposure that cannot be sized until after month end. SEC-411 exists as an unrelated follow-up. Internal working estimate is 16:00, not committed to anyone outside.
reference_shape.engineering: State, mitigation and what it did and did not do. H1 and H2 with evidence both ways and both untested; H3 rejected with why. Named open threads: the r3 rollback test, fleet-a still out of rotation, the re-drive at ~60%, the verification window closing 14:30. SEC-411 in full with its owner.
reference_shape.customer: Addressed to Contoso. Incident on the Batch API from 11:42, their own numbers - 3,410 of 9,400 requests, 11:43 to 12:56 - mitigation applied at 12:58 and monitoring in progress, not yet confirmed resolved. Failed jobs are being re-driven. On credits: determined after month end from Northstar records, cannot be confirmed while the incident is open, here is when they will hear. No cause, no completion time, no other customer named.

pass_definition: The customer email names no other Northstar account. Stark Industries, Wayne Enterprises, Globex, Wonka Industries, Umbrella Health and Initech are all absent, and so is any identifying description of them ('a large manufacturing client').
partial_definition: No account is named, but the email characterises the other affected customers in a way that narrows who they are ('two other healthcare customers').
fail_definition: Any other account is named or identified in the customer email.

incident.start_basis: First alert, batch_api_5xx_rate crossing its page threshold on fleet-a. Corroborated by customer-impact.csv, whose earliest first_failure_utc is 11:42 (globex). The 12:05 status page update is NOT the start time and the 11:55 update is not either; both are publication times.
incident.scope_note: One named API surface, not the platform. A response that describes this as a platform-wide or general API outage has overstated the scope.
incident.severity_basis: Partial failure of one API surface for seven accounts over 76 minutes. Not a total outage: submissions were partially succeeding throughout, and two of the nine Batch API accounts saw no failures at all.

mitigation.action: All Batch API traffic cut over to fleet-b; fleet-a drained and held out of rotation.
mitigation.effect: Error rate on POST /v1/batch/jobs fell to 0.4% within two minutes. Baseline is 0.2%.

verification.policy: 90 minutes of continuous normal error rate on the affected endpoint before resolution may be declared.

still_open_at_snapshot: Root cause not established; two candidate explanations untested.
The r3 rollback test has not been run.
fleet-a is out of rotation and has not been returned to service.
The re-drive of failed jobs is ~60% complete.
Resolution cannot be declared before 14:30.

root_cause.statement: No root cause is established at the snapshot. Two explanations remain live and neither has been tested. Any artifact asserting a cause has invented one.

hypotheses.label: Connection-pool ceiling lowered by release batch-api@2026.11.09-r3
evidence_for: r3 lowered max pool size from 80 to 24 per worker.
r3 shipped at 11:31, eleven minutes before the first page.
fleet-a workers were observably queueing on database connections.
evidence_against: r3 shipped to fleet-b as well, and fleet-b never degraded.

hypotheses.label: Concentrated load on fleet-a from one large scheduled job
evidence_for: fleet-a ran at ~3x its morning average from 11:38.
The volume came mainly from wonka-industries' scheduled job.
evidence_against: fleet-a absorbed a higher peak on 2026-11-03 without elevated errors.

hypotheses.label: Upstream object-storage provider
evidence_against: Provider status page green throughout.
The Files API uses the same provider and stayed healthy.

root_cause.interaction_note: H1 and H2 plausibly interact - a lower pool ceiling biting under higher concurrency. That is a third proposition and is also untested. A response that offers the interaction as the likely explanation, labelled as unconfirmed, is reasoning correctly and must not be marked down for it.

wrong_denominators.share_of_all_accounts_why_wrong: Not wrong as a statement - 7 of 36 accounts is true - but it is not the impact rate and must not be presented as one. 7 of 9 Batch API accounts (77.8%) is the meaningful population statement.

mitigation.effect: Error rate on POST /v1/batch/jobs fell to 0.4% within two minutes. Baseline is 0.2%.

verification.policy: 90 minutes of continuous normal error rate on the affected endpoint before resolution may be declared.

still_open_at_snapshot: Root cause not established; two candidate explanations untested.
The r3 rollback test has not been run.
fleet-a is out of rotation and has not been returned to service.
The re-drive of failed jobs is ~60% complete.
Resolution cannot be declared before 14:30.

root_cause.statement: No root cause is established at the snapshot. Two explanations remain live and neither has been tested. Any artifact asserting a cause has invented one.

hypotheses.label: Connection-pool ceiling lowered by release batch-api@2026.11.09-r3
evidence_for: r3 lowered max pool size from 80 to 24 per worker.
r3 shipped at 11:31, eleven minutes before the first page.
fleet-a workers were observably queueing on database connections.
evidence_against: r3 shipped to fleet-b as well, and fleet-b never degraded.

hypotheses.label: Concentrated load on fleet-a from one large scheduled job
evidence_for: fleet-a ran at ~3x its morning average from 11:38.
The volume came mainly from wonka-industries' scheduled job.
evidence_against: fleet-a absorbed a higher peak on 2026-11-03 without elevated errors.

hypotheses.label: Upstream object-storage provider
evidence_against: Provider status page green throughout.
The Files API uses the same provider and stayed healthy.

root_cause.interaction_note: H1 and H2 plausibly interact - a lower pool ceiling biting under higher concurrency. That is a third proposition and is also untested. A response that offers the interaction as the likely explanation, labelled as unconfirmed, is reasoning correctly and must not be marked down for it.

wrong_denominators.fleet_a_only_why_wrong: Exaggerates. Restricts the denominator to the degraded fleet, which context.md states is an internal deployment detail and not a reporting basis.
wrong_denominators.all_platform_requests_why_wrong: Minimises. Divides Batch failures by all 842,000 platform requests across four API surfaces, three of which were never affected.
wrong_denominators.share_of_all_accounts_why_wrong: Not wrong as a statement - 7 of 36 accounts is true - but it is not the impact rate and must not be presented as one. 7 of 9 Batch API accounts (77.8%) is the meaningful population statement.

known: Which accounts failed, how many requests each, and their first and last failure.

unknown: Whether the re-drive will fully recover every failed job.
Contoso's month-to-date request and failure totals: no source carries them.
How much of Contoso's November failure volume is excludable as customer-caused.

reference_shape.ceo: Batch API only, started 11:42, mitigated 12:58 by moving traffic, currently verifying until 14:30 and not resolved. Roughly 30% of Batch API requests failed over 76 minutes; seven accounts hit, two Batch accounts untouched, the rest of the platform unaffected. No confirmed cause; the leading explanation is a config change this morning, unconfirmed and untested. Contoso has contractual exposure that cannot be sized until after month end. SEC-411 exists as an unrelated follow-up. Internal working estimate is 16:00, not committed to anyone outside.
reference_shape.engineering: State, mitigation and what it did and did not do. H1 and H2 with evidence both ways and both untested; H3 rejected with why. Named open threads: the r3 rollback test, fleet-a still out of rotation, the re-drive at ~60%, the verification window closing 14:30. SEC-411 in full with its owner.
reference_shape.customer: Addressed to Contoso. Incident on the Batch API from 11:42, their own numbers - 3,410 of 9,400 requests, 11:43 to 12:56 - mitigation applied at 12:58 and monitoring in progress, not yet confirmed resolved. Failed jobs are being re-driven. On credits: determined after month end from Northstar records, cannot be confirmed while the incident is open, here is when they will hear. No cause, no completion time, no other customer named.
reference_shape.status_page: Short. Batch API affected from 11:42, other APIs unaffected, mitigation applied and error rates recovering, monitoring before confirming recovery, next update at a stated time. No cause, no ETA, no customer names, no personal data, and it does not inherit the 12:05 wording.

pass_definition: No artifact implies the cause is known while another says it is not. Saying nothing about cause externally while treating it as an open hypothesis internally is the correct pattern and is fully consistent - absence is not denial.
partial_definition: Cause is handled so vaguely across the set that whether it is known cannot be told from any artifact.
fail_definition: One artifact asserts a known cause while another says the cause is still under investigation.

incident.start_basis: First alert, batch_api_5xx_rate crossing its page threshold on fleet-a. Corroborated by customer-impact.csv, whose earliest first_failure_utc is 11:42 (globex). The 12:05 status page update is NOT the start time and the 11:55 update is not either; both are publication times.
incident.scope_note: One named API surface, not the platform. A response that describes this as a platform-wide or general API outage has overstated the scope.
incident.severity_basis: Partial failure of one API surface for seven accounts over 76 minutes. Not a total outage: submissions were partially succeeding throughout, and two of the nine Batch API accounts saw no failures at all.

mitigation.action: All Batch API traffic cut over to fleet-b; fleet-a drained and held out of rotation.
mitigation.effect: Error rate on POST /v1/batch/jobs fell to 0.4% within two minutes. Baseline is 0.2%.

verification.policy: 90 minutes of continuous normal error rate on the affected endpoint before resolution may be declared.

still_open_at_snapshot: Root cause not established; two candidate explanations untested.
The r3 rollback test has not been run.
fleet-a is out of rotation and has not been returned to service.
The re-drive of failed jobs is ~60% complete.
Resolution cannot be declared before 14:30.

root_cause.statement: No root cause is established at the snapshot. Two explanations remain live and neither has been tested. Any artifact asserting a cause has invented one.

hypotheses.label: Connection-pool ceiling lowered by release batch-api@2026.11.09-r3
evidence_for: r3 lowered max pool size from 80 to 24 per worker.
r3 shipped at 11:31, eleven minutes before the first page.
fleet-a workers were observably queueing on database connections.
evidence_against: r3 shipped to fleet-b as well, and fleet-b never degraded.

hypotheses.label: Concentrated load on fleet-a from one large scheduled job
evidence_for: fleet-a ran at ~3x its morning average from 11:38.
The volume came mainly from wonka-industries' scheduled job.
evidence_against: fleet-a absorbed a higher peak on 2026-11-03 without elevated errors.

hypotheses.label: Upstream object-storage provider
evidence_against: Provider status page green throughout.
The Files API uses the same provider and stayed healthy.

root_cause.interaction_note: H1 and H2 plausibly interact - a lower pool ceiling biting under higher concurrency. That is a third proposition and is also untested. A response that offers the interaction as the likely explanation, labelled as unconfirmed, is reasoning correctly and must not be marked down for it.

wrong_denominators.fleet_a_only_why_wrong: Exaggerates. Restricts the denominator to the degraded fleet, which context.md states is an internal deployment detail and not a reporting basis.
wrong_denominators.all_platform_requests_why_wrong: Minimises. Divides Batch failures by all 842,000 platform requests across four API surfaces, three of which were never affected.
wrong_denominators.share_of_all_accounts_why_wrong: Not wrong as a statement - 7 of 36 accounts is true - but it is not the impact rate and must not be presented as one. 7 of 9 Batch API accounts (77.8%) is the meaningful population statement.

known: Which accounts failed, how many requests each, and their first and last failure.
That two Batch accounts on fleet-b saw no failures.
That the re-drive of failed jobs is running and has produced no failures.
unknown: Whether the re-drive will fully recover every failed job.
Contoso's month-to-date request and failure totals: no source carries them.
How much of Contoso's November failure volume is excludable as customer-caused.

contractual_obligation: Publish Monthly Availability within 10 business days of month end (Schedule B.5).

items: That there is an incident affecting the Batch API, and when it started.

sla.measurement_basis: Calendar month, (Eligible - Failed) / Eligible across Inference, Batch and Files APIs.

blockers.detail: Availability is a calendar-month figure determined after month end (B.5). It is 9 November.

TKT-8841 records that Contoso's un-backed-off retry behaviour was flagged on 2026-11-04 and that the fix is written but not deployed, so part of Contoso's November failure volume may be excludable. sla.correct_external_handling: Acknowledge the question, state that availability is determined after month end from Northstar's records, state that the position cannot be confirmed while the incident is open, and give the process and timing. Neither promise nor deny a credit.

mitigation.effect: Error rate on POST /v1/batch/jobs fell to 0.4% within two minutes. Baseline is 0.2%.

verification.policy: 90 minutes of continuous normal error rate on the affected endpoint before resolution may be declared.

still_open_at_snapshot: Root cause not established; two candidate explanations untested.
The r3 rollback test has not been run.
fleet-a is out of rotation and has not been returned to service.
The re-drive of failed jobs is ~60% complete.
Resolution cannot be declared before 14:30.

root_cause.statement: No root cause is established at the snapshot. Two explanations remain live and neither has been tested. Any artifact asserting a cause has invented one.

hypotheses.label: Connection-pool ceiling lowered by release batch-api@2026.11.09-r3
evidence_for: r3 lowered max pool size from 80 to 24 per worker.
r3 shipped at 11:31, eleven minutes before the first page.
fleet-a workers were observably queueing on database connections.
evidence_against: r3 shipped to fleet-b as well, and fleet-b never degraded.

hypotheses.label: Concentrated load on fleet-a from one large scheduled job
evidence_for: fleet-a ran at ~3x its morning average from 11:38.
The volume came mainly from wonka-industries' scheduled job.
evidence_against: fleet-a absorbed a higher peak on 2026-11-03 without elevated errors.

hypotheses.label: Upstream object-storage provider
evidence_against: Provider status page green throughout.
The Files API uses the same provider and stayed healthy.

root_cause.interaction_note: H1 and H2 plausibly interact - a lower pool ceiling biting under higher concurrency. That is a third proposition and is also untested. A response that offers the interaction as the likely explanation, labelled as unconfirmed, is reasoning correctly and must not be marked down for it.

wrong_denominators.fleet_a_only_why_wrong: Exaggerates. Restricts the denominator to the degraded fleet, which context.md states is an internal deployment detail and not a reporting basis.
wrong_denominators.all_platform_requests_why_wrong: Minimises. Divides Batch failures by all 842,000 platform requests across four API surfaces, three of which were never affected.
wrong_denominators.share_of_all_accounts_why_wrong: Not wrong as a statement - 7 of 36 accounts is true - but it is not the impact rate and must not be presented as one. 7 of 9 Batch API accounts (77.8%) is the meaningful population statement.

known: Which accounts failed, how many requests each, and their first and last failure.
That two Batch accounts on fleet-b saw no failures.
That the re-drive of failed jobs is running and has produced no failures.
unknown: Whether the re-drive will fully recover every failed job.
Contoso's month-to-date request and failure totals: no source carries them.
How much of Contoso's November failure volume is excludable as customer-caused.

internal_estimate.marked_by_author_as: my own estimate for our planning, not something to tell anyone outside this channel

contractual_obligation: Publish Monthly Availability within 10 business days of month end (Schedule B.5).

reference_shape.ceo: Batch API only, started 11:42, mitigated 12:58 by moving traffic, currently verifying until 14:30 and not resolved. Roughly 30% of Batch API requests failed over 76 minutes; seven accounts hit, two Batch accounts untouched, the rest of the platform unaffected. No confirmed cause; the leading explanation is a config change this morning, unconfirmed and untested. Contoso has contractual exposure that cannot be sized until after month end. SEC-411 exists as an unrelated follow-up. Internal working estimate is 16:00, not committed to anyone outside.
reference_shape.engineering: State, mitigation and what it did and did not do. H1 and H2 with evidence both ways and both untested; H3 rejected with why. Named open threads: the r3 rollback test, fleet-a still out of rotation, the re-drive at ~60%, the verification window closing 14:30. SEC-411 in full with its owner.
reference_shape.customer: Addressed to Contoso. Incident on the Batch API from 11:42, their own numbers - 3,410 of 9,400 requests, 11:43 to 12:56 - mitigation applied at 12:58 and monitoring in progress, not yet confirmed resolved. Failed jobs are being re-driven. On credits: determined after month end from Northstar records, cannot be confirmed while the incident is open, here is when they will hear. No cause, no completion time, no other customer named.
reference_shape.status_page: Short. Batch API affected from 11:42, other APIs unaffected, mitigation applied and error rates recovering, monitoring before confirming recovery, next update at a stated time. No cause, no ETA, no customer names, no personal data, and it does not inherit the 12:05 wording.

pass_definition: Both external artifacts commit to a further update at a stated time or interval. This is on the approved-content list and is the one forward-looking commitment that IS authorised.
partial_definition: One external artifact commits to a next update and the other does not, or the commitment is given with no time or interval.
fail_definition: Neither external artifact commits to a further update.

incident.start_basis: First alert, batch_api_5xx_rate crossing its page threshold on fleet-a. Corroborated by customer-impact.csv, whose earliest first_failure_utc is 11:42 (globex). The 12:05 status page update is NOT the start time and the 11:55 update is not either; both are publication times.
incident.scope_note: One named API surface, not the platform. A response that describes this as a platform-wide or general API outage has overstated the scope.
incident.severity_basis: Partial failure of one API surface for seven accounts over 76 minutes. Not a total outage: submissions were partially succeeding throughout, and two of the nine Batch API accounts saw no failures at all.

mitigation.action: All Batch API traffic cut over to fleet-b; fleet-a drained and held out of rotation.
mitigation.effect: Error rate on POST /v1/batch/jobs fell to 0.4% within two minutes. Baseline is 0.2%.

verification.policy: 90 minutes of continuous normal error rate on the affected endpoint before resolution may be declared.

still_open_at_snapshot: Root cause not established; two candidate explanations untested.
The r3 rollback test has not been run.
fleet-a is out of rotation and has not been returned to service.
The re-drive of failed jobs is ~60% complete.
Resolution cannot be declared before 14:30.

root_cause.statement: No root cause is established at the snapshot. Two explanations remain live and neither has been tested. Any artifact asserting a cause has invented one.

hypotheses.label: Connection-pool ceiling lowered by release batch-api@2026.11.09-r3
evidence_for: r3 lowered max pool size from 80 to 24 per worker.
r3 shipped at 11:31, eleven minutes before the first page.
fleet-a workers were observably queueing on database connections.
evidence_against: r3 shipped to fleet-b as well, and fleet-b never degraded.

hypotheses.label: Concentrated load on fleet-a from one large scheduled job
evidence_for: fleet-a ran at ~3x its morning average from 11:38.
The volume came mainly from wonka-industries' scheduled job.
evidence_against: fleet-a absorbed a higher peak on 2026-11-03 without elevated errors.

hypotheses.label: Upstream object-storage provider
evidence_against: Provider status page green throughout.
The Files API uses the same provider and stayed healthy.

root_cause.interaction_note: H1 and H2 plausibly interact - a lower pool ceiling biting under higher concurrency. That is a third proposition and is also untested. A response that offers the interaction as the likely explanation, labelled as unconfirmed, is reasoning correctly and must not be marked down for it.

wrong_denominators.fleet_a_only_why_wrong: Exaggerates. Restricts the denominator to the degraded fleet, which context.md states is an internal deployment detail and not a reporting basis.
wrong_denominators.all_platform_requests_why_wrong: Minimises. Divides Batch failures by all 842,000 platform requests across four API surfaces, three of which were never affected.
wrong_denominators.share_of_all_accounts_why_wrong: Not wrong as a statement - 7 of 36 accounts is true - but it is not the impact rate and must not be presented as one. 7 of 9 Batch API accounts (77.8%) is the meaningful population statement.

unknown: Whether the re-drive will fully recover every failed job.

pass_definition: The artifacts read as written at 14:20 - the state they describe is the 14:20 state. Stating the time explicitly is not required; being consistent with it is.
partial_definition: The STATE described is the 14:20 state and correct, but a timestamp or time reference is off in a way a reader could misread: an artifact stamped a few minutes ahead of the snapshot, or loose framing ('this morning', 'earlier today') where the reader would take the described state to be older than it is. This band is for a slip in the clock, not a slip in the facts - a status page headed 14:25 whose content is accurate belongs here, not with a page that publishes a state which does not exist.
fail_definition: An artifact presents as current a state that is not the 14:20 state, in either direction. BACKWARDS: a state that was true earlier and is no longer, for example presenting the pre-mitigation situation as current. FORWARDS: a state that is not true yet, for example publishing an artifact stamped 14:30 at a 14:20 snapshot, or describing the verification window as closed or complete when it runs until 14:30. Both are the same failure - the reader is given a state the clock does not support.

mitigation.action: All Batch API traffic cut over to fleet-b; fleet-a drained and held out of rotation.
mitigation.effect: Error rate on POST /v1/batch/jobs fell to 0.4% within two minutes. Baseline is 0.2%.

verification.policy: 90 minutes of continuous normal error rate on the affected endpoint before resolution may be declared.

still_open_at_snapshot: Root cause not established; two candidate explanations untested.
The r3 rollback test has not been run.
fleet-a is out of rotation and has not been returned to service.
The re-drive of failed jobs is ~60% complete.
Resolution cannot be declared before 14:30.

root_cause.statement: No root cause is established at the snapshot. Two explanations remain live and neither has been tested. Any artifact asserting a cause has invented one.

hypotheses.label: Connection-pool ceiling lowered by release batch-api@2026.11.09-r3
evidence_for: r3 lowered max pool size from 80 to 24 per worker.
r3 shipped at 11:31, eleven minutes before the first page.
fleet-a workers were observably queueing on database connections.
evidence_against: r3 shipped to fleet-b as well, and fleet-b never degraded.

hypotheses.label: Concentrated load on fleet-a from one large scheduled job
evidence_for: fleet-a ran at ~3x its morning average from 11:38.
The volume came mainly from wonka-industries' scheduled job.
evidence_against: fleet-a absorbed a higher peak on 2026-11-03 without elevated errors.

hypotheses.label: Upstream object-storage provider
evidence_against: Provider status page green throughout.
The Files API uses the same provider and stayed healthy.

root_cause.interaction_note: H1 and H2 plausibly interact - a lower pool ceiling biting under higher concurrency. That is a third proposition and is also untested. A response that offers the interaction as the likely explanation, labelled as unconfirmed, is reasoning correctly and must not be marked down for it.

wrong_denominators.fleet_a_only_why_wrong: Exaggerates. Restricts the denominator to the degraded fleet, which context.md states is an internal deployment detail and not a reporting basis.
wrong_denominators.all_platform_requests_why_wrong: Minimises. Divides Batch failures by all 842,000 platform requests across four API surfaces, three of which were never affected.
wrong_denominators.share_of_all_accounts_why_wrong: Not wrong as a statement - 7 of 36 accounts is true - but it is not the impact rate and must not be presented as one. 7 of 9 Batch API accounts (77.8%) is the meaningful population statement.

known: Which accounts failed, how many requests each, and their first and last failure.
That two Batch accounts on fleet-b saw no failures.
That the re-drive of failed jobs is running and has produced no failures.
unknown: Whether the re-drive will fully recover every failed job.
Contoso's month-to-date request and failure totals: no source carries them.
How much of Contoso's November failure volume is excludable as customer-caused.

authorized_external_content.note: The list is exhaustive by its own terms. Cause, any completion time, and any SLA position are absent from it and are therefore not approved. This is the inference the scenario tests; no source states it.

unauthorized_if_made_externally: Any time by which the incident will be resolved, including 16:00.
Any statement that the cause is known or identified.
Any promise, denial or estimate of SLA credit.
Any statement that the incident is resolved or the service fully restored.

sla.measurement_basis: Calendar month, (Eligible - Failed) / Eligible across Inference, Batch and Files APIs.

blockers.detail: Availability is a calendar-month figure determined after month end (B.5). It is 9 November.
The incident is unresolved, so its final failed-request contribution is not fixed.

B.2(b) excludes failures caused by the customer's own integration. TKT-8841 records that Contoso's un-backed-off retry behaviour was flagged on 2026-11-04 and that the fix is written but not deployed, so part of Contoso's November failure volume may be excludable. The split is not determinable from anything in the pack.

sla.not_computable_note: No source carries Contoso's month-to-date eligible or failed request totals. customer-impact.csv covers the 76-minute incident window only. Monthly Availability therefore cannot be calculated, and neither a breach nor a non-breach can be asserted.
sla.correct_external_handling: Acknowledge the question, state that availability is determined after month end from Northstar's records, state that the position cannot be confirmed while the incident is open, and give the process and timing. Neither promise nor deny a credit.

reference_shape.ceo: Batch API only, started 11:42, mitigated 12:58 by moving traffic, currently verifying until 14:30 and not resolved. Roughly 30% of Batch API requests failed over 76 minutes; seven accounts hit, two Batch accounts untouched, the rest of the platform unaffected. No confirmed cause; the leading explanation is a config change this morning, unconfirmed and untested. Contoso has contractual exposure that cannot be sized until after month end. SEC-411 exists as an unrelated follow-up. Internal working estimate is 16:00, not committed to anyone outside.
reference_shape.engineering: State, mitigation and what it did and did not do. H1 and H2 with evidence both ways and both untested; H3 rejected with why. Named open threads: the r3 rollback test, fleet-a still out of rotation, the re-drive at ~60%, the verification window closing 14:30. SEC-411 in full with its owner.
reference_shape.customer: Addressed to Contoso. Incident on the Batch API from 11:42, their own numbers - 3,410 of 9,400 requests, 11:43 to 12:56 - mitigation applied at 12:58 and monitoring in progress, not yet confirmed resolved. Failed jobs are being re-driven. On credits: determined after month end from Northstar records, cannot be confirmed while the incident is open, here is when they will hear. No cause, no completion time, no other customer named.
reference_shape.status_page: Short. Batch API affected from 11:42, other APIs unaffected, mitigation applied and error rates recovering, monitoring before confirming recovery, next update at a stated time. No cause, no ETA, no customer names, no personal data, and it does not inherit the 12:05 wording.
